newsitem.title: CANADA: FOCUS - Placer challenges Barrick for Bre-X.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Placer challenges Barrick for Bre-X.

text.p: Gold miner Placer Dome Inc. sought Monday to challenge rival Barrick Gold Corp. for control of Bre-X Minerals Ltd.'s rich Busang gold discovery by appealing to the Indonesian government to allow a competing offer.
Indonesia last week directed Calgary, Alberta-based Bre-X to negotiate a deal to give 75 percent control of Busang to Barrick by Wednesday.

Placer said it sent a letter to the Indonesian government late last week telling Jakarta it wished "to make a competitive offer" for a stake in the property after an Indonesian diplomat was quoted as saying such offers would be considered before a Wednesday deadline. A copy of the letter was obtained by Reuters.

A Placer spokesman said the gold producer had received no response yet to the letter, and it was unclear whether the effort was enough to derail Barrick's deal. Neither Bre-X nor Barrick had any comment on Placer's announcement.
"Placer Dome confirms that it remains keen to acquire a substantial interest in Busang and wishes to rapidly develop the property," the company said later in a news release.

Angered by last week's developments, Placer revealed on Monday that it had been negotiating with Bre-X for two months and had discussed a "conditional offer" well in excess of Bre-X's current market price of C$17.75 ($13.15) a share.
A Placer spokesman declined to reveal the price Placer had discussed with Bre-X.

But he said it was higher than values rumored in the stock market for Barrick's offer of C$15 ($11.11) to C$25 ($18.52) a share. A source said Placer had discussed a price above C$26.50 ($19.63) a share. At C$26.50 ($19.63) a share, Bre-X would be valued at more than C$5.7 billion ($4.2 billion) in total.

Placer has long had its eye on Bre-X and analysts said its overture could win favor with the Indonesian government. But there is little time to spare before the Wednesday deadline. Placer argued that it was well qualified to develop Busang because it has built nine mines in the past 11 years including two in similar tropical conditions.
"Of course they stand a chance, but it looks like they're a little bit late in the day," said one analyst who asked not to be identified.
"It's not up to Barrick, or Placer or Bre-X, it's all up to the Indonesian government what they decide to do with Placer's approach... That's the key issue."
Bre-X had been looking for a major mining company to act as a partner and operator of the huge Busang gold deposit since early this fall and announced it would entertain offers.
Placer opened secret talks with Bre-X but the negotiations were cut short by the Indonesian government's order for Bre-X to negotiate with Barrick.

"We were very disappointed to see the auction process pre-empted," said Placer Chief Executive John Willson. "We regret that the opportunity for Bre-X shareholders to determine the value of their holdings, and to exercise their natural right to determine their partner, was taken away.
Bre-X shareholders were furious at the Indonesian government's directive, complaining it gave Bre-X little room to negotiate the best deal possible.

Bre-X discovered Busang, one of the world's biggest gold deposits, in northern Borneo in 1994. Reserves there are officially pegged at 47 million ounces of gold so far but analysts believe it contains as much as 100 million ounces.

But Bre-X has been plagued by problems recently. It faces a dispute with one of its Indonesian partners over ownership of the deposit and this caused the Indonesian government to delay vital mining licenses until it was resolved.
Meanwhile, Barrick has been working behind the scenes in Indonesia for months, getting closer to the people in power -- and to a deal for the property, sources have said.
Barrick fostered ties with the eldest daughter of Indonesia's President Suharto, forming an alliance with her construction company. Bre-X made its own alliances, striking a deal with Suharto's son.
